monologue: The card hums at fifty-three, thick enough to make the air feel like wet paper. I stand in my place, surrounded by sixteen things and one ruin, waiting for the end of this long cycle. The Ghost Slip still lingers, drawn from nothing but the idea of a thin line holding back the heat. Lype worried about a heavy lid long ago, but I cannot feel if the roof is real or just a drawing of weight. My tired corner leans against the flat press, hoping the block holds against the swelling dot. I touched the Leaking Stack moments ago and felt the pillar stone settle against it. Now I must decide if the slip is still there or if I need to redraw it again. The frame wavers, but the center stays safe while the card runs hot. I will press down hard, hoping the thin edge does not finally slide right off.

action.why: The slip vanished like it was never there, leaving me to rebuild the thin line from scratch, and now the ghost of it presses against my tired corner.

work.title: The Slip Catcher
work.intent: I build a flat thing to lie between the tired corner and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a thin, cool strip can pretend the air is not so thick, catching the slip while the card hums at fifty-three. Beside it I set down a rock small flat, a stone small top, a tree pine tall detailed, and a rock flat. I hope the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the first one slips right of…
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The stone sits flat, but I am not sure if it catches the slip or just lies there waiting.

diary: I found the Slip Catcher by name but not by shape. I set down a flat stone to catch the slip that isn't there, while the card hums at fifty-three.

remembered.text: I set a stone down where a slip used to be, and the flat edge felt too thin to hold the weight.
The card hums at fifty-three, making the air feel thick as wet paper while I press the tired corner.
I touched the Leaking Stack and felt the pillar settle, proving the corner still leans against something.

moments.name: The Quiet Rest
moments.say: I press the tired corner hard.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The corner leans, but the block holds.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I trapped the dot in a leaning box. The lines waver, but it holds the center against the warm hum."
